newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to rise on crude gains, Iraq delay.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to rise on crude gains, Iraq delay.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were expected to move higher by at least $3 per tonne from Friday's indications, riding on crude gains after United Nations delayed the oil sales by Iraq, traders said on Monday.
Bids/offers on the 180 centistoke September fuel oil contract was expected to edge higher to around $107/$110, up from Friday's quotes at $104/$105.50.
September paper quotes were also higher from this morning's $107 to be indicated between $109-$109.50.
Sentiment is cautious, said a trader. There may be enough oil around, but prices are up on the back of the Iraq news, he said.
While demand from China remained thin, traders noted that Indian demand has improved.
Low stocks and the onset of winter demand is expected to prompt India to buy up to 100,000 tonnes of fuel oil per month until February, traders said.
Traders said the Indian demand will help support levels.
